source.publisher: Deutscher Akademischer Austauschdienst (DAAD) - German Academic Exchange Service
source.raw_extract: If you wish to apply for a DAAD scholarship, please read the call for applications for your chosen scholarship programme in the scholarship database, paying particular attention to application deadlines. The scholarship database will take you to the application portal.
source.exact_deadline_wording: please read the call for applications for your chosen scholarship programme in the scholarship database, paying particular attention to application deadlines
source.notes: No single official DAAD deadline exists for a record generically titled 'DAAD Scholarship'. DAAD operates ~150 distinct scholarship programmes (research grants, Master's scholarships, STEM study scholarships, EPOS, Hilde Domin, In-Country/In-Region), each with its own closing date published only inside its own Call for Applications in the scholarship database. DAAD's own overview page redirects applicants to per-programme calls for deadlines. Writing any single date for this umbrella record would require picking one arbitrary programme out of the database, which the contract forbids (AGENT_BRIEF section 5: a generic deadline for a different programme; section 6: no cycle assumptions). The record is too coarse-grained to resolve to one programme. I did not consult any individual programme's database detail page, because choosing which of the 150 programmes this generic record represents would itself be an invention.

records.title: Deutschlandstipendium (Germany Scholarship)
records.deadline_display: Zum jeweiligen Verfahren und den Fristen erkundigen Sie sich direkt an Ihrer Hochschule.

source.publisher: Bundesministerium fuer Forschung, Technologie und Raumfahrt (BMFTR) - Deutschlandstipendium
source.raw_extract: 4. Bewerben Sie sich Reichen Sie Ihre Bewerbung mit den geforderten Nachweisen an Ihrer Hochschule ein. Zum jeweiligen Verfahren und den Fristen erkundigen Sie sich direkt an Ihrer Hochschule.
source.exact_deadline_wording: Zum jeweiligen Verfahren und den Fristen erkundigen Sie sich direkt an Ihrer Hochschule.
source.notes: The federal programme deliberately centralises neither the application procedure nor the deadlines. The official BMFTR guidance states positively that applicants must enquire with their own university about the procedure AND the deadlines ('Fristen'). This is affirmative official evidence that no federal deadline exists for this record, not merely missing evidence. The programme FAQ corroborates the delegation: 'Die Auswahlverfahren werden im Einzelnen durch die Hochschulen festgelegt und bekanntgemacht. Die Stipendien werden oeffentlich ausgeschrieben.' Classification note: this is UNKNOWN rather than ROLLING or ANNUAL because BMFTR never says 'rolling' or 'no fixed deadline' - it says the deadline belongs to a third party (each university). Per AGENT_BRIEF section 6, differing deadlines across the ~700 participating universities is explicitly NOT a CONFLICTING case, so CONFLICTING is not used. No date can be written, and per section 5 I did not borrow any single university's Deutschlandstipendium deadline.

records.title: Amsterdam Merit Scholarship (AMS)
records.deadline_display: Applications should be submitted to the Admissions Offices of the Graduate Schools. Deadlines for the AMS differ per Faculty or Graduate School.

source.raw_extract: Applications should be submitted to the Admissions Offices of the Graduate Schools. Deadlines for the AMS differ per Faculty or Graduate School. You can find the specific eligibility requirements, selection criteria and application instructions on the Faculty or Graduate School websites.
source.exact_deadline_wording: Deadlines for the AMS differ per Faculty or Graduate School.
source.notes: The record's own official_source_url is dead (HTTP 404); I used the record's catalogue_url instead, which is the live official AMS page. That page publishes NO date and states affirmatively that the AMS deadline is faculty- or graduate-school-specific. Since the record is the institution-wide AMS rather than a named faculty's AMS, there is no single deadline to write. The Faculty of Science page does say 'The application deadline is 15 January' for its single AMS award for the September 2027 start, but that is one faculty's AMS allocation and AGENT_BRIEF section 5 bars using another programme's deadline for this record. Note also that '15 January' on that page carries no year, so even if it were in scope it could not yield a YYYY-MM-DD without a cycle assumption (section 6). Not classified CONFLICTING: per section 6, different faculties of one institution having different deadlines is not a conflict.

records.title: Google PhD Fellowship Program
records.deadline_display: Applications are currently closed for the 2026 cycle. - Applications open March 5, 2026 - Applications close April 30, 2026

source.raw_extract: ## Application status Applications are currently closed for the 2026 cycle. - Applications open March 5, 2026 - Applications close April 30, 2026 - Notification of proposal decisions by Aug. 31, 2026 - Public announcement of new fellowship recipients by Oct. 31, 2026
source.notes: This is the clearest case in the shard and still does not yield a writable date. The official page states an explicit calendar closing date of 2026-04-30 for the 2026 cycle, and states in the present tense that 'Applications are currently closed'. As of retrieval on 2026-10-05 that closing date is roughly five months in the past, and the record is carried in the open/upcoming gap set. Per AGENT_BRIEF section 6, a clearly-past deadline on an open/upcoming record is outcome expired_mismatch: the stale date must not be written and must not be silently rolled forward to 2027. Google has published no 2027 cycle dates, so no substitute date exists. deadline_semantics is recorded as EXACT because that is genuinely what the source states (an explicit calendar deadline); deadline_date is null solely because of the past-date rule, and the unextracted value is preserved out-of-band in withheld_past_deadline. The two later 2026 milestones (Aug. 31 and Oct. 31 2026) are also past or imminent but are notification dates, not the application deadline, so they are not candidates. Not ROLLING: the page does not say rolling or no fixed deadline. Not CONFLICTING: only one official source was needed and none disagrees.

records.title: Toloa Tertiary Scholarship (Toloa Scholarships - tertiary stream, Ministry for Pacific Peoples)
records.deadline_display: Tertiary scholarship applications closed at 5pm on Monday 9 February 2026.

source.publisher: Ministry for Pacific Peoples, New Zealand Government
source.as_of: 2026 academic year (400 secondary and 10 tertiary scholarships)
source.raw_extract: Applications for 2026 tertiary scholarships are now closed There are 400 secondary scholarships and 10 tertiary scholarships on offer for the 2026 academic year. Secondary scholarship applications closed at 5pm on Friday 23 January 2026. Tertiary scholarship applications closed at 5pm on Monday 9 February 2026.
source.exact_deadline_wording: Tertiary scholarship applications closed at 5pm on Monday 9 February 2026.
source.notes: The tertiary stream is stated separately from the secondary stream, and only the tertiary figure is relevant to this record: 5pm on Monday 9 February 2026. The page states in the present tense that 'Applications for 2026 tertiary scholarships are now closed'. As of retrieval on 2026-10-05 that date is roughly eight months past, and the record sits in the open/upcoming gap set with verification_status 'needs_review'. Per AGENT_BRIEF section 6 this is outcome expired_mismatch: the stale date is not written and not silently moved to the 2027 round, which the Ministry has not published. deadline_semantics is EXACT because the source genuinely states an explicit calendar deadline; deadline_date is null only because of the past-date rule, with the unextracted value preserved out-of-band in withheld_past_deadline. The secondary deadline of 23 January 2026 is explicitly not used - it belongs to a different stream of the same scheme. Not ROLLING and not ANNUAL: the page gives a fixed date for a named year, not recurring timing. Not CONFLICTING: a single official page states both dates unambiguously. Note also that the page records that the Ministry funds the scheme but 'Le Va manages the application process', so the application portal itself is a third-party administrator, not an official government portal - it was not needed and was not consulted.
